Ahold Delhaize stock faces 2026 outlook cut after cyber incident
sum: Ahold Delhaize reported resilient third-quarter results on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, but lowered parts of its full-year outlook after an October cybersecurity incident disrupted online services and Benelux supply-chain operations. The company said in its Q3 release that it expects the incident to weigh on fourth-quarter performance.
Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 35.87 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:31 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026, 1.58% above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12, at 35.31 euros.

The retailer estimates that the October incident will reduce fourth-quarter net sales by between 200 million euros and 250 million euros. Underlying and IFRS operating income are expected to decline by between 75 million euros and 100 million euros, while additional response and remediation costs should have a marginal effect on 2026 IFRS operating income.

The company now expects diluted underlying earnings per share growth at constant exchange rates in the low single digits, compared with its previous mid- to high-single-digit forecast. Free cash flow is projected at around 2.1 billion euros, down from at least 2.3 billion euros previously. The underlying operating margin is still expected to approach 4.0%, versus earlier guidance of around 4.0%.

Management said the incident mainly affected online capabilities in the Benelux and the United States, as well as Benelux supply-chain operations. Bol was not affected. Most of the disruption was contained within two weeks, but work to restore normal operations continued after the quarter ended.

Third-quarter net sales rose 1.9% at constant exchange rates and 2.6% at actual exchange rates to 23.1 billion euros. Online sales increased 8.2% at constant exchange rates, led by 14.2% growth in the United States, the tenth consecutive quarter of double-digit U.S. online growth.

Underlying operating margin was 4.1%, down 0.1 percentage points at constant exchange rates. Diluted underlying earnings per share rose 1.4% at constant exchange rates to 0.69 euros. IFRS operating income reached 976 million euros, 30 million euros above underlying operating income, mainly because of a pension settlement in the U.S.

Ahold stock steadies after cyber incident cuts 2026 outlook
sum: Ahold Delhaize reported resilient third-quarter results on November 4, but the Dutch food retailer lowered its 2026 outlook after an October cybersecurity incident disrupted parts of its online and supply-chain operations. The company said in its November 4 results release that quarterly net sales increased 1.9 percent at constant exchange rates to 23.1 billion euros.

Ahold stock traded at 35.38 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:02 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026, 0.45 percent above the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 11. Investing.com identifies the relevant Xetra instrument as AHOG and showed a closing price of 35.22 euros for November 11.

Comparable sales excluding gasoline rose 1.2 percent across the group. Europe was the stronger region, with comparable sales up 2.1 percent and sales increasing 3.1 percent at constant exchange rates to 9.8 billion euros. In the United States, comparable sales excluding gasoline rose 0.5 percent, while sales increased 1.1 percent at constant exchange rates to 13.3 billion euros.

Online sales increased 8.2 percent at constant exchange rates, led by 14.2 percent growth in the United States. Management said this was the tenth consecutive quarter of double-digit U.S. online growth. The group underlying operating margin was 4.1 percent, down 0.1 percentage points at constant exchange rates, while diluted underlying earnings per share rose 1.4 percent to 0.69 euros.

The reported figures included a 976 million euro IFRS operating income and diluted IFRS earnings per share of 0.72 euros. The company said IFRS operating income was 30 million euros above the underlying figure, mainly because of a pension settlement in the U.S. Third-quarter free cash flow reached 445 million euros.

Ahold Delhaize expects the October incident to reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million to 250 million euros and underlying and IFRS operating income by 75 million to 100 million euros. The company said most disruption was contained within two weeks, but restoration work was continuing when the results were published.
Management now expects 2026 underlying operating margin to approach 4.0 percent, compared with previous guidance of around 4.0 percent.

items.t: Ahold Delhaize stock adds Tesco deal as cyber hit cuts outlook
sum: Ahold Delhaize added a new European expansion move to its updated 2026 outlook on Wednesday, November 4. The supermarket group agreed to acquire 100% of Tesco's operations in Czechia and Slovakia, subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory clearances, according to the Ahold Delhaize newsroom.

Following completion, the company expects its Albert brand and Tesco Czechia to form the leading grocery retail brand in Czechia by market share. Ahold Delhaize also expects to become a significant player in Slovakia. The transaction fits the group's stated focus on in-market and adjacent-market opportunities, where it already has operational presence and brand recognition.

The October cybersecurity incident affected online capabilities in the Benelux and the United States as well as parts of the Benelux supply chain. Management expects the disruption to reduce fourth-quarter net sales by 200 million to 250 million euros and underlying and IFRS operating income by 75 million to 100 million euros. Response and remediation costs are expected to have a marginal impact on 2026 IFRS operating income.

Ahold Delhaize now expects diluted underlying earnings per share to grow at a low-single-digit rate at constant exchange rates, compared with its previous mid- to high-single-digit forecast. Free cash flow is expected at about 2.1 billion euros, versus at least 2.3 billion euros previously. The company also plans to begin a 1 billion euro annual share buyback program in 2027.

Third-quarter net sales rose 1.9 percent at constant exchange rates to 23.1 billion euros. Online sales increased 8.2 percent, driven by 14.2 percent growth in the United States, while the underlying operating margin reached 4.1 percent. The company said most of the cyber disruption was contained within two weeks, although work to restore normal operations continues.
Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 34.28 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:03 CET on Monday, November 9, 0.26 percent above the Xetra close of Monday, November 9.

NCR Voyix Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
sum: NCR Voyix VYX reported a 20% decline in third-quarter revenue as it transitioned its hardware business, while growth in recurring software revenue and a jump in the value of contracts for its Voyix Commerce Platform offered signs of progress in its software strategy.
The company also promoted Darren Wilson to president, putting the retail and restaurant businesses under his leadership, and said its Aloha Next restaurant product had gone live at its first site.

Revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30 fell to $539 million. Excluding the hardware transition, revenue declined 3%, primarily because of lower hardware and related installation services, partially offset by 1% growth in recurring revenue, Chief Financial Officer Brian Webb-Walsh said.

NCR Voyix reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance but said it now expects revenue at the lower end of its previously issued range because of delayed hardware purchases and related installation revenue.

The company added 10 contracts for its embedded Voyix Commerce Platform, or VCP, applications during the quarter, bringing the total number of customers to 35. Remaining contract value reached $440 million, up 151% from a year earlier and 54% sequentially.

Chief Executive Officer Jim Kelly highlighted six enterprise customer signings during the quarter but cautioned that the pace of contract growth may vary. “I don’t expect every quarter to be of this magnitude,” he said.

Among the retail agreements, NCR Voyix renewed its first VCP contract with Ahold Delhaize USA, which Wilson said has more than 1,000 live trading lanes across over 100 stores. The customer is continuing to roll out the grocery and fuel software across its 29,000 lanes. The company also announced expanded agreements with A.S. Watson and Rutter’s, and a VCP agreement with Cencosud in Argentina.

Results: Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize N.V. Exceeded Expectations And The Consensus Has Updated Its Estimates
sum: Investors in Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize N.V. (AMS:AD) had a good week, as its shares rose 4.5% to close at €34.22 following the release of its quarterly results. It looks like a credible result overall - although revenues of €23b were in line with what the analysts predicted, Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize surprised by delivering a statutory profit of €0.72 per share, a notable 14% above expectations. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize's 16 analysts is for revenues of €96.1b in 2027. This reflects a credible 4.4% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to increase 6.5% to €2.81. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of €95.8b and earnings per share (EPS) of €2.88 in 2027. So it looks like there's been a small decline in overall sentiment after the recent results - there's been no major change to revenue estimates, but the analysts did make a small dip in their earnings per share forecasts.

It might be a surprise to learn that the consensus price target was broadly unchanged at €37.44, with the analysts clearly implying that the forecast decline in earnings is not expected to have much of an impact on valuation. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize at €44.00 per share, while the most bearish prices it at €22.63. There are definitely some different views on the stock, but the range of estimates is not wide enough as to imply that the situation is unforecastable, in our view.

items.t: Ahold Delhaize Earnings Call: Growth Meets Cyber Risk
[Ahold Delhaize Q3 2026 Earnings Call] Cyberattack to Cut €200-250M from Q4 Sales, Full-Year Margin Outlook Trimmed to ~4%
sum: Ahold Delhaize reported third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, but the headline was overshadowed by a cybersecurity incident that struck in October, forcing the retailer to take systems offline and prompting a downgrade to its full-year outlook. The company now expects an underlying operating margin approaching 4%, down from previous guidance, and free cash flow of around €2.1 billion, a €200 million reduction.

CEO Frans Muller opened the call by addressing the cyber incident directly. "We apologize to our customers for the disruption and inconvenience and are grateful for their trust, loyalty, and understanding," he said. "Cyber threats are an increasingly harsh reality of doing business today."

CFO Jolanda Poots-Bijl quantified the impact: Q4 net sales will be reduced by €200-250 million, and underlying operating income by €75-100 million. Approximately 80% of the sales hit is in Europe, particularly the Netherlands, while the profit impact is more balanced due to mitigation efforts. The incident affected online capabilities in the Benelux and U.S., as well as parts of the Benelux supply chain, though bol was not impacted.

"The underlying operating income impact is based on many elements next to the regular sales flow-through. For example, it's shrink, extra hours worked to get supply running, promotional actions to welcome our customers back, and the negative impact on, for example, lost vendor allowances and retail media," Poots-Bijl explained.

Despite the cyber overhang, the underlying quarter showed resilience. Net sales rose 1.9% to €23.1 billion, helped by a 15 basis point positive impact from weather and calendar shifts. Underlying operating margin dipped 10 basis points to 4.1%, as a favorable discounting effect on insurance provisions at group level was offset by a modest decline in the U.S. Diluted underlying EPS increased 1% to €0.69, supported by higher operating profit and share buybacks, partially offset by higher financial expenses.

Cyberattack on supermarket fridges spreads across Europe, spoils food stocks
sum: The latest cyberattack, which echoed a similar incident in France last month, targeted supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg and Ireland.

A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize, and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.
"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."
A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems."

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

sum: Ahold Delhaize stock traded lower on Monday as investors looked ahead to the group's third-quarter results on November 4. The latest company calendar confirms the release date, while the share has moved materially below the level cited in the previous report.

Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 31.98 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 2:39:20 p.m. CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 2.53 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The comparison uses the Friday Xetra close of 32.81 euros identified for the AHOG listing by De Belegger.

Since the previous October 30 report, which cited a Lang & Schwarz price of 33.13 euros, the share has declined 3.47 percent. This is a market comparison rather than a statement about the cause of the move.

Ahold Delhaize's investor-relations calendar lists third-quarter 2026 results for November 4, 2026. The company published its second-quarter results on August 5, making the upcoming release the next scheduled checkpoint for revenue, profitability and the outlook.

The results will be particularly relevant for investors tracking the group's operating margin and sales momentum. A fresh quarter should show whether the trends discussed ahead of the release are reflected in reported performance.

On October 30, Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak businesses to Ahold Delhaize. The transaction covers stores, offices and distribution centres in both countries, while Tesco's Hungarian operations are excluded.

Completion requires antitrust and other regulatory approvals and is expected in the second half of 2027. Tesco expects to return most net proceeds through an additional share buyback after completion and expects the transaction to be broadly neutral to earnings per share and its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio after the buyback.

Ahold Delhaize stock faces margin test before November 4 results
sum: Ahold Delhaize is due to publish its third-quarter results on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The update will give investors a fresh read on trading in the United States and Europe after concerns about softer volumes and falling food prices in the Netherlands.
Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 32.95 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:06 CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Ahold Delhaize stock.

RBC Capital Markets expects profit margins to tighten in the third quarter, according to Finimize. The bank cited softer US grocery volumes, Dutch food-price deflation and pressure on fresh-produce sales.

RBC models a combined 1.6 percentage-point hit to third-quarter performance from reduced US food-aid benefits, egg-price deflation and changes affecting pharmacy profits under the Inflation Reduction Act. The bank also cut its price target to 37 euros from 38 euros and reduced longer-term forecasts for underlying pretax profit, dividend per share and earnings per share by 1% to 2%.

The results should show how Ahold Delhaize balances traffic, promotions and profitability when lower prices limit the contribution from inflation. The key operating questions are whether US demand stabilized and whether the Dutch business protected volumes without giving up too much margin.

Ahold Delhaize posts Q4 earnings beat, misses on full year
sum: Ahold Delhaize reported higher sales and profit for the 2025 financial year on Wednesday but missed earnings expectations, even as it posted a fourth-quarter underlying operating income beat and raised its dividend.

The Netherlands-based supermarket group generated net sales of €92.35bn for the year, broadly in line with the €92.31bn consensus, while net income attributable to common shareholders rose to €2.26bn from €1.76bn.
However, both net income and EPS came in below expectations of €2.36bn and €2.62 respectively.
In the fourth quarter, sales rose to €23.5bn from €23.28bn a year earlier, slightly ahead of analyst estimates of around €23.34bn.

Underlying operating income reached €994m, exceeding the €918m expected by analysts, supported by a strong performance in the United States, where the group operates chains including Stop & Shop, Giant, Food Lion and Hannaford, alongside Albert Heijn and Delhaize in the Netherlands and Belgium.
Free cash flow increased 2.2% to €2.6bn in 2025, driven by underlying earnings, though the company expects this to ease to at least €2.3bn in 2026.
The group proposed a final dividend of €0.73 per share, taking the full-year payout to €1.24, up from €1.17 previously.
